extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry familiar with Mochizuki's IUT framework
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and structural properties (ring/integral structures, monoids, Kummer correspondences, log-volumes, Frobenioid constructions) for tensor packets, processions, and associated LGP/lgp monoids in the IUT (Mochizuki) framework. Focuses on local/global compatibilities, normalisations, and algorithms to build Frobenioids from local data.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1-tensor packet and j-tensor packet assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall refer to the assignment V_Q 3 v_Q 7! log(F_vQ) := ⊕_{V3v j v_Q} log(F_v) as the 1-tensor packet associated to the F-prime-strip F, and the assignment V_Q 3 v_Q 7! log(S_j F_vQ) := ⊗_{i∈S_j} log(F_vQ) the j-tensor packet associated to the collection {F} where the tensor product is taken as a tensor product of ind-topological modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the basic packet objects: 1-tensor packet is a direct sum of local logs; j-tensor packet is the tensor product (of ind-topological modules) of the involved factors. Use these as the canonical objects when forming local/global tensor constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring Structures (local holomorphic tensor packets)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Ring Structures) The ind-topological field structures on log(F_v) for i∈S_j determine an ind-topological ring structure on log(S_j F_vQ) as an inductive limit of direct sums of ind-topological fields. Such decompositions are compatible with the natural action of the topological group (i)(5)_v on the direct summand with subscript v of the factor labelled i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When forming j-tensor packets one must propagate the local ind-topological field structures to obtain a global ind-topological ring; verify compatibility with the indicated topological group actions on summands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral Structures (local holomorphic tensor packets)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Integral Structures) For i∈S_j define ind-topological submodules log(S_{j+1;(i)} F_v) := log(F_v)_{j+1,v} etc. Then the ind-topological submodule log(S_{j+1;(i)} F_v) forms a direct summand of the ind-topological ring log(S_{j+1;(i)} F_v), which is also an inductive limit of direct sums of ind-topological fields. Moreover, by forming the tensor product with 1’s in the factors labelled by indices not equal to i, we obtain a natural injective homomorphism log(F_v) → log(S_{j+1;(i)} F_v). In particular the integral structure log(F_v)[:] determines integral structures on each of the direct summand ind-topological fields appearing in the inductive limit descriptions of log(S_{j+1;(i)} F_v), log(S_{j+1} F_vQ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integral structures are defined via direct-summand submodules and injections obtained by tensoring with units in other factors; check inductive limit descriptions and appropriate choices in the limits to obtain isomorphisms onto direct summands. These integral structures propagate to tensor packets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic / Holomorphic Compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: (Mono-analytic/Holomorphic Compatibility) When a D'-collection arises from an F-collection, the poly-isomorphisms log(yF_v) tauto! log(yF'_{v}\Kum"poly) and corresponding isomorphisms log(F_vQ) tauto! log(F'_{vQ}) \Kum"poly ! log(D'_{vQ}) induce compatibilities log(S_j F_vQ) tauto! log(S_j F'_{vQ}) \Kum"poly ! log(S_j D'_{vQ}) and similarly for j+1; i.e., mono-analytic structures and holomorphic structures are related by the indicated poly-isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure poly-isomorphisms induced by log-links and the Kummer-type identifications hold; these are the compatibility conditions needed to transfer structures between holomorphic and mono-analytic contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral Structures (mono-analytic / D' context)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Integral Structures) For V containing v j v_Q the étale-like mono-analytic log-shells determine topological submodules I(D'_{vQ}) ⊂ log(D'_{vQ}); I(S_j D'_{vQ}) ⊂ log(S_j D'_{vQ}); I(S_{j+1;(i)} D'_v) ⊂ log(S_{j+1;(i)} D'_v) which can be regarded as integral structures on the Q-spans. For Archimedean v_Q, regard the log-shells as closed unit balls of Hermitian metrics on log(yD'_v) and induced Hermitian metrics on the tensor/direct-sum spaces so that their closed unit balls serve as integral structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build integral structures in mono-analytic contexts either via étale-like log-shells (non-Arch) or via Hermitian metric closed unit balls (Arch), then take Q-spans to compare with holomorphic integral structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global j-tensor packet and localisation homomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: (Ring Structures) The field structures on (yM_mod)_S_j determine a ring structure on (yM_mod)_S_j which decomposes as a direct sum of number fields. By composing with given log-links, the localisation functors (yM_mod)_j → yF_j of Corollary 11.23 give a natural injective localisation ring homomorphism gl: to loc: ! log(S_{j+1} F_{VQ}) := ∏_{v_Q∈VQ} log(S_{j+1} F_{vQ}) to the product of the local holomorphic tensor packets, where the component labelled by 0 in log(S_{j+1} F_{vQ}) is defined to be 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the global level construct the global j-tensor packet (yM_mod)_S_j and verify the injective localisation homomorphism into the product of local packets, taking care of the labelling/0-component convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global integral-structure compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: (Integral Structures) For each i∈S_j, by tensoring with 1’s in the factors labelled by indices not equal to i, we obtain a natural injective ring homomorphism (yM_mod)_i → (yM_mod)_S_j which induces isomorphisms of the domain onto subfields of each direct summand of the codomain. For each v_Q∈Vnon (resp. Varc), the composite (yM_mod)_i → (yM_mod)_S_j → log(S_{j+1} F_{vQ}) sends the ring of integers (resp. elements of absolute value 1 for all Archimedean primes) of (yM_mod)_i into the integral structures on log(S_{j+1} F_{vQ}) (resp. in the Archimedean direct-summand ind-topological fields).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global-to-local compatibility requires that global rings of integers / unit loci map into the previously defined local integral structures; check compatibility of the injections with the local integral structures and labellings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Packet Monoids
rubrics_metrics.description: (Single Packet Monoids) For v with v j v_Q, the image of the monoid log(F_v), its submonoid of units, and its realification via the natural homomorphism log(F_v) → log(S_{j+1;(i)} F_v) determine monoids log(S_{j+1;(i)} F_v); (units) log(S_{j+1;(i)} F_v); R log(S_{j+1;(i)} F_v) which are equipped with G_v((i)(5)_v)-actions when v∈V_non, and for the first monoid, with a pair of an Aut-holomorphic orbispace and a Kummer structure when v∈V_arc. These monoids are regarded as (possibly realified) subquotients of log(S_{j+1;(i)} F_v) which act on appropriate subquotients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When passing from single F_v monoids to their images in packet-level objects, record the induced group actions (Galois-type) and any Aut/Kummer structures for Archimedean places; treat these monoids as actors on suitable subquotients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Logarithmic Gaussian Procession Monoids (FLGP)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Local Logarithmic Gaussian Procession Monoids) Given a log-link zHT→yHT and the F-prime-strip processions Proc(yF_T), the Frobenius-like Gaussian monoid Fgau(yHT(2))_v is defined by submonoids in the product over j of log(j; zF_v). Pulling back via the poly-isomorphism given by the log-link and sending to the isomorphism constructed in (1) yields a functorial algorithm (w.r.t. the log-link) to construct collections of monoids (log(j; zF_v))_j equipped with splittings up to torsion when v∈V_bad (resp. splittings when v∈V_good). These are called Frobenius-like local LGP-monoids or Frobenius-like local logarithmic Gaussian procession monoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction is algorithmic and functorial in the log-link; one must check splittings at bad primes (up to torsion) and actual splittings at good primes. Use the Foil-symmetrising compatibility to perform the construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertically coric local LGP-monoids and associated Kummer theory
rubrics_metrics.description: (Vertically Coric Local LGP-Monoids and Associated Kummer Theory) From a Gaussian log-theta-lattice collection of Hodge theatres one defines D-(2)(1)-Hodge theatres n;◦HT and associated F(n;◦D)_t prime-strips. Applying the constructions of Proposition 13.6(2) to full log-links produces functorially collections of monoids (LGP(n;◦HT D)_v) equipped with splittings up to torsion at v∈V_bad (resp. splittings at v∈V_good). For each n,m the algorithm is compatible with the algorithm of Proposition 13.6(2) via Kummer isomorphisms cns(...)_F_t Kum! cns(...)_D_t; one obtains Kummer isomorphisms of local LGP-monoids for all v∈V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the vertical-coricity construction: ensure that the Kummer identifications are established and that the functoriality in n,m and compatibility with existing constructions is verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semi-compatibility (non-Archimedean primes)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Upper Semi-Compatibility — non-Archimedean Primes) For v_Q∈V_non the Kummer isomorphism Kum composed with the m0-th iteration of the p_v-adic logarithm log^{m0} sends labeled components ((cns(n;mF)_{jtj}))^{n;m}_v into the integral modules I_Q(S_{j+1} F(n;◦D)_vQ). More precisely, Kum ◦ log^{m0}(((cns(n;mF)_{jtj})) )^{n;m}_v ⊂ I_Q(S_{j+1} F(n;◦D)_vQ) for m0≥0, considering the iteration only for elements whose (m0−1)-iteration lies in the unit group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At non-Archimedean primes check that iterated p-adic logarithmic parts of log-links composed with Kummer send the designated labeled monoid components into the specified integral submodules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semi-compatibility (Archimedean primes)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Upper Semi-Compatibility — Archimedean Primes) For v_Q∈V_arc the Kummer isomorphism Kum composed with the m0-th iteration of the Archimedean exponential part of the log-link places the labeled components into vertically coric closed unit balls I(S_{j+1} F(n;◦D)_vQ), possibly as closed balls of a specified radius δ inside cns(...). For m0≥0 one considers the m0-th iteration only for elements whose (m0−1)-iteration lies in the unit group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At Archimedean primes verify images land in the closed unit balls determined as integral structures by Hermitian metrics; keep track of radii/normalisations and which iterates are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semi-compatibility (bad primes) and indeterminacy control
rubrics_metrics.description: (Bad Primes) For v∈V_bad the monoids FLGP, LGP come equipped with natural splittings up to torsion (or up to 2^l-torsion). Denote the splitting submonoids from these splittings by (?), and consider their actions on ind-topological modules I_Q(S_{j+1;j}F(n;◦D)_v). The only possible relations between these actions via log-links are indeterminacies coming from multiplication by roots of unity in the domains of log-links. The p_v-adic logarithm portion of the log-link sends the indeterminacies at m (multiplication by roots) to addition by zero at m+1, i.e., removes the indeterminacy at the next step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At bad primes expect splittings only up to torsion; track multiplicative indeterminacies by roots of unity and verify that p-adic logarithm iteration removes these indeterminacies at the next level (m→m+1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of global (pre-)Frobenioids from local data
rubrics_metrics.description: (Single Packet Global non-Realised Frobenioid) From the image of the number field via the homomorphisms of Proposition 13.5 one has a functorial algorithm to construct a (pre-)Frobenioid (yF~_MOD)(i) := Im((yM_mod)_S_j → log(S_{j+1} F_{VQ})). There are natural isomorphisms between the constructed objects and their modular/realification versions. The construction uses local fractional ideals and produces tautological isomorphisms on associated rational function monoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Globally assemble local packet data via the localisation homomorphisms to produce pre-Frobenioids; verify the induced identifications on rational function monoids and the behaviour of local fractional ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global reified LGP/lgp Frobenioids and dependence on log-links
rubrics_metrics.description: (Global Realised Logarithmic Gaussian Procession Frobenioids) Given a log-link zHT→yHT, the above constructions can be carried out in a z-labelled manner producing reified LGP/lgp Frobenioids ((z!)yC)_LGP and corresponding F-prime-strips (z!)yF_LGP (and lgp variants) together with natural tautological isomorphisms. The realiﬁed constructions fit into commutative diagrams relating realiﬁed and non-realiﬁed categories and localisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a log-link is present, carry the labelling through construction; ensure naturality with respect to localisation isomorphisms and the commutative diagrams between reified and non-reified versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot and q-pilot object definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: (Definition of pilot/q-pilot) Regard an object of the global reified Frobenioid (z!)yC_LGP determined by any collection indexed by v∈V_bad of generators (up to torsion) of the monoids (?)Flgp((z log) yHT)_v as a (2)-pilot object. The object of the global reified Frobenioid determined by any collection of generators up to torsion of the splitting monoid associated to the split Frobenioid in the v-component is called a q-pilot object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are naming conventions for global objects generated by local (splitting) generators; useful when tracking how chosen generators produce global Frobenioid objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full poly LGP-link and LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: (Full poly-links and lattices) A full poly-isomorphism (full poly LGP-link) from one Hodge theatre to another, relative to a log-link, is the object called a full poly LGP-link (resp. lgp-link). A diagram of such full log-links arranged in the Gaussian log-theta-lattice (n,m indices) is called the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice (resp. lgp-Gaussian log-theta-lattice). Both types of links send (2)-pilot objects to q-pilot objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions provide the combinatorial/diagrammatic framework (lattice of log-links) used to relate multiple Hodge theatres; verify that links map pilot→q-pilot objects as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packet-normalisation and Procession-normalisation for log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: (Local Holomorphic Packets — Log-volumes) For V 3 v j v_Q the p_{v_Q}-adic log-volume (resp. radial log-volume) on each direct summand field of I_Q(F_vQ), I_Q(S_{j+1;j}F_vQ) with the normalised weights determines log-volumes M(I_Q(...)) → R such that the log-volume of each of the local holomorphic integral structures given by the integral structures of Proposition 13.3(2) is equal to zero. This normalisation is called the packet-normalisation. When working with collections of capsules in a procession, normalise log-volumes on products associated to various capsules by taking the average over the capsules; this is the procession-normalisation. The normalisation is invariant under permutations of S_j (and capsules). The normalisation is chosen so multiplication by p_v corresponds to ± log(p_v) on the log-volume (packet-normalisation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When defining log-volumes choose packet-normalisation so integral structures have zero log-volume and choose procession-normalisation by averaging over capsules; check behaviour under multiplication by p_v and invariance under permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic compatibility of log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: (Mono-analytic Compatibility) By applying the p_vQ-adic (or radial) log-volume of Proposition 12.2(4) and adjusting the discrepancy between the local holomorphic integral structures and the mono-analytic integral structures, one obtains log-volumes on the mono-analytic log-shells \IyD'_{v} and the corresponding I_Q(S_j D'_{vQ}), I_Q(S_{j+1;(i)} D'_v) etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To compare/transport log-volumes from holomorphic packets to mono-analytic shells, explicitly compute and adjust discrepancies between the two integral-structure choices so the induced log-volumes agree as specified.
